Hi Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and items we promised to follow up on from the call: 

1) PII scope: you mentioned customer names, account numbers (masked in UI), and limited payment metadata. Can you confirm whether any raw PAN / full card numbers or unmasked SSNs are ever sent to our service?

2) Retention windows: you said transaction-level records are kept for 7 years for compliance but operational logs are shorter. Can you confirm the retention window you require for: request logs, audit logs, and cached model context?

3) Support access model: you asked about break-glass and least-privilege for our support engineers. We outlined role-based access (scoped, ephemeral) in the demo — Ben will attach the RBAC matrix and break-glass flow. Please let us know which support roles at ClearBank need read vs write vs debug shell access.

4) Logging & evidence: you requested SOC 2 evidence and examples of audit logs for support activity. I've attached a high-level SOC 2 index for reference (we'll follow up with the SOC 2 pack via our security portal if helpful).

Next steps: 
- Jordan: confirm the PII types and which retention windows are non-negotiable for you (due by EOW if possible).
- Priya (if included): any regulatory constraints we should be aware of (local data residency, transfer restrictions)?
- Ben/Monica: prepare RBAC matrix + break-glass runbook for review and a short exported audit-log sample (redacted).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up if easier.

Best,
Hannah

Hannah — thanks for the clear notes and the demo. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- PII: we do NOT send raw PANs or full SSNs to vendors. Anything card-related is tokenized by our gateway. The dataset used for model context may include account_id and masked account numbers (e.g., ****1234).

- Retention: regulatory requires transaction records stored for 7 years (archival), but operational logs we can tolerate shorter retention. Our minimums: request logs (90 days), audit logs for access events (3 years) — the latter is non-negotiable for OLAR audits.

- Support roles: we have a small support ops team that needs read-only access for troubleshooting (view request payloads, trace IDs). A different SRE group may need elevated debug access in emergencies. Break-glass should be reserved for SRE and require an approval flow (ticket + 2nd approver).

- SOC 2: happy to get particulars; Priya is included to own anything regulatory/security. Priya — can you confirm whether we need EU data residency for any of the workloads?

Jordan
Jordan Hale

Jordan / Hannah — following up from the technical side with concrete notes and the RBAC attachment. High level: 

- RBAC model (attached: redwood-support-rbac-matrix.xlsx): roles we typically map for enterprise customers: 
  * read_only_support — view traces, request/response payloads (PII redaction enforced at the transport layer)
  * support_debug — ephemeral debug sessions (obfuscated shell, no direct DB creds)
  * sre_oncall — elevated, time-limited debug + ability to forward traces to storage for deep analysis
  * admin — config and policy change only (very restricted)

- Break-glass flow: 
  * Initiated by ticket (Jira/ServiceNow) + escalation via PagerDuty. 
  * Temp access token issued for scoped session (max TTL 2 hours). 
  * All activity recorded to immutable audit log (append-only) and forwarded to your SIEM for retention. 
  * Two-person approval recommended for elevation (requestor + approver).

- Logs & retention: 
  * Request logs (including trace ID, timestamp, request metadata): default retention 90 days; can be extended to 365 days per contract.
  * Audit logs (user access, role changes, break-glass events): stored for 3 years by default for enterprise plans; we support export to your S3 or a partner SIEM for long-term retention.

- Evidence & encryption: SOC 2 pack (index attached) + example audit snippet (redacted) available. Data in transit encrypted TLS 1.2+; at rest encryption AES-256 with customer-managed KMS support for Private deployments.

Attachments: redwood-support-rbac-matrix.xlsx, soc2-evidence-index.pdf

If helpful, I can produce a short export demonstrating an actual break-glass session (redacted trace + timeline) to show the audit trail.

—Ben
